The head arm passes six more ids than the base, which are the node's six new cases in tests/test_spawn_retries_a_vanished_bind.py (the base arm cannot contain them: the file does not exist at a31484ff0). The head arm ran at 9bf13264b rather than the run head c81adfd6f, and that gap is benign: c81adfd6f touches only docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/spawn-retries-a-vanished-bind.html and its figure, so the code under the gate is byte-identical at both revisions. The reviewer independently reproduced the head tree green (9 passed EXIT=0, tests/test_spawn_retries_a_vanished_bind.py + tests/test_fence_protects_the_worktree_pool.py) with the module under test resolving to reckon/crew/dispatch.py of the reviewed worktree.

findings.text: Commit 04538bea5 reformats eleven unrelated pre-existing regions of dispatch.py (hunks at lines 418, 644, 2890, 4204, 5670, 7793, 9293, 9818, 9901, 9940, 10245) alongside the three feature hunks (7885, 7905, 8644), so the dispatch.py diff is +176/-71 while the feature itself is the ~104 inserted retry lines. Verified by ruff: git show a31484ff0:reckon/crew/dispatch.py is '1 file would be reformatted' and the head file is '1 file already formatted'. The repo's rule is that a sweep is its own commit because folding mechanical reformatting into a feature makes both unreviewable; here it obscures where the feature begins and ends. It does not change behaviour and adds no lint finding (ruff check is 7 at base and 7 at head over the changed paths), so it does not hold the node.

The startup window that decides whether a child 'started' is PROTECTED_BIND_WAIT_INTERVAL_SECONDS (0.05 s), and the primary test widens it to 250 ms (TEST_WINDOW_SECONDS, tests/test_spawn_retries_a_vanished_bind.py), so neither the test nor the gate exercises the shipped 50 ms value. On a loaded host a real bwrap refusing over a vanished source could take longer than 50 ms to exit; the poll would then see a still-running child and treat it as a successful start, and the retry the node exists to provide would not fire. The failure this defends against is a rename window that is itself shorter than 50 ms, so the margin is plausibly large enough, but the shipped value is unverified and worth a follow-on measurement rather than a change here.

item_verdicts.control: The pool-control repair is sound and needed: at a31484ff0 the fence already composed from _backends.declared_protected_paths (reckon/_backends.py:2923), but _without_pool patched _backends.protected_paths, the narrower exists()-filtered view the fence does not read, so the declared mutation stripped nothing and the pool's read-only overlay stayed in the argv. The head versions of _without_pool and _negative_control_report patch declared_protected_paths, and the node's new test_the_pool_control_driver_mutation_reaches_the_fence proves the mutation reaches the composed argv (_ro_bind_of==-1 after the patch, !=-1 before).
item_verdicts.diff: Read all three commits against a31484ff0 end to end. 04538bea5 is the feature: the retry helpers and both seam wrappings, the collected-exit record, and the pool-control-driver repair in tests/test_fence_protects_the_worktree_pool.py. 9bf13264b makes the startup check tolerate a non-pollable launch stand-in. c81adfd6f adds only the evidence fragment and figure. The feature logic is ~104 inserted lines of dispatch.py plus 376 lines of new tests; the dispatch.py diff reads +176/-71 because 04538bea5 also reformats eleven unrelated pre-existing regions (see findings). No plan, sprint or shared-index file is touched.
item_verdicts.done_when: Every clause holds. (1) A spawn that fails with bwrap's bind error naming a protected path retries bounded by the same named constants: the bound is _backends.PROTECTED_BIND_WAIT_ATTEMPTS and the sleep is _backends.PROTECTED_BIND_WAIT_INTERVAL_SECONDS (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7963-7968), the constants §31's composition wait uses. (2) The retry precedes the failure record: _spawn_detached_worker computes the retried process and only then reads the collected exit (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8025-8034) or registers the pid; the refused try is neither recorded nor registered. (3) A spawn failing for another reason is not retried: _died_over_a_vanished_bind_source returns False unless the child exited nonzero inside the window with a matching stderr (test test_a_spawn_that_fails_for_another_reason_is_not_retried asserts one process and the recorded failure). (4) A test simulates a first try refused and a second that starts and asserts one launched attempt: test_a_spawn_refused_over_a_vanished_protected_bind_is_retried asserts len(spawn.processes)==2, the first try reaped, pid==last, launch_failures empty and phase still working; parametrized over both refusal phrases. (5) A second case asserts an unrelated failure is not retried. (6) The negative control removes the retry and the first case then fails to launch (neg-control-bind-2.log, EXIT=1, the two refused-phrase ids).
item_verdicts.goal: The observable goal is met at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7945-7973: _spawn_worker_retrying_a_vanished_bind takes the attempt callable, calls it once, and while tries remain and the just-spawned child died over a missing bind source (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7910-7943) it reaps the dead try, sleeps PROTECTED_BIND_WAIT_INTERVAL_SECONDS, and calls attempt() again, bounded by max(1, _backends.PROTECTED_BIND_WAIT_ATTEMPTS). Recognition is keyed to the launch's own bind sources: _read_only_bind_sources (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7893-7901) parses the argv's --ro-bind SRC DEST words, and _refusal_names_a_bind_source (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7903-7908) requires both a bwrap refusal phrase and one of those sources in the text. Both spawn seams route through it: _spawn_detached_worker (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7974) and _supervisor_spawn_worker (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8739).

justifications.durability: The guard is shown firing: test_the_retry_stops_at_the_named_attempt_bound drives a refusal that outlives the bound and asserts exactly PROTECTED_BIND_WAIT_ATTEMPTS processes, the earlier tries reaped, and one recorded launch failure; the negative control removes the retry and the first case fails. The node also repaired a negative control that had been inert since §31 (the fence composes from declared_protected_paths, not the narrower protected_paths the old _without_pool patched), so the pool control now actually exercises what it claims. Deducted one for the window question recorded under findings: the primary test widens the shipped window, so the 50 ms production value is not itself exercised.
justifications.evidence: Both gate arms carry an EXIT line and a summary line and stamp their own revision in the header (gate-base-bind.log 'revision=a31484ff0', 11 passed EXIT=0; gate-head-bind-2.log 'revision=9bf13264b', 17 passed EXIT=0), the head adds no failing id, the six new cases are separately exercised, the declared negative control is red with the two refused-phrase ids (neg-control-bind-2.log EXIT=1), and the reviewer reproduced the head tree green independently. Deducted one because the base arm log (gate-base-bind.log) is a git-archive scratch tree but records only the revision, not the module-under-test path and resolved cwd the scratch-tree header convention asks for, so the base arm's identity rests on the revision stamp alone.
justifications.fit: The helpers sit with the other spawn code, follow the module's existing shape, name the mechanism ('vanished bind', read-only bind sources) rather than any plan or ticket, and their comments state the why (why a rename leaves a window, why the startup poll collects an exit it must then record). Deducted two: the same eleven-hunk reformatting bloats the diff and makes the intended change harder to isolate, and the startup window reuses the composition interval constant as a timeout, which conflates a retry interval with a startup budget.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The observable goal is met and pinned: a spawn refused over a bind source this launch mounted is retried within a bounded retry loop (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7945-7973), keyed to the launch's own --ro-bind sources rather than to any bind text (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7903-7908, with the test's positive control at tests/test_spawn_retries_a_vanished_bind.py asserting str(resolved_destination(protected)) in _read_only_bind_sources(argv)), bounded by the constants §31's composition wait uses, and a non-bind failure is returned unchanged for its caller to record.
justifications.scope_discipline: The five declared paths are the only ones changed and no plan or shared index is edited. Deducted two because commit 04538bea5 folds a file-wide formatter sweep into the feature: eleven hunks of pure reformatting of pre-existing code (reckon/crew/dispatch.py lines 418, 644, 2890, 4204, 5670, 7793, 9293, 9818, 9901, 9940, 10245) sit beside the three feature hunks, and base dispatch.py is 'would be reformatted' while head is 'already formatted' under ruff format --check, so the churn is a whole-file format run folded into a fix commit rather than landed alone.
